title: Streaming observability pipeline: chunk-level tracing, adaptive redaction, and client compatibility shim
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers using streaming responses (chat/generation and function/tool call streams) need better visibility into per-chunk behavior (latency, size, failure), distributed tracing that ties chunk events to request spans, and a way to prevent streaming content from leaking secrets in logs or downstream observability stores.

Goal: Implement an end-to-end observability pipeline for streamed outputs that provides: 1) per-chunk metrics and histograms, 2) tracing spans that represent chunk lifecycle (enqueue -> started -> emitted -> acked), and 3) an adaptive redaction layer that removes sensitive substrings before any persisted logs/metrics while keeping structured outputs usable for downstream evals. Also provide a lightweight client compatibility shim so older SDKs can opt into the new chunk telemetry without breaking integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Chunk-level telemetry emitted for >95% of streamed requests: chunk_index, emit_time_ms, chunk_size_bytes, tokens_in_chunk, client_stream_id
Tracing spans created per-chunk with parent request span and exported to Jaeger/OTLP with sampling consistent across request and chunks

Redaction rules applied before persistence: redact API keys, bearer tokens, 16+ digit numeric sequences, and customer-specified regex patterns; redaction log must be reversible only by KMS-authorized personnel (metadata flag), not present in plaintext in logs
SDK compatibility shim implemented for Node and Python SDKs exposing opt-in streaming.trace=true flag and backward-compatible fallbacks
Dashboards updated: per-route chunk size distribution, chunk latency P50/P95/P99, percent of chunks redacted, and top-10 redaction patterns
Feature-flagged rollout with canary to 1% of hosted traffic and automated fallback to previous pipeline on error
Performance overhead <5% p50 latency increase for stream-enabled routes when pipeline is enabled
implementation_notes:
High-level plan: (1) Instrument runtime emitter to attach chunk metadata and emit OTLP events; (2) Add a thin middleware in the streaming stack to create child spans for each chunk lifecycle event; (3) Implement redaction as a streaming transform that operates on tokens/chunk text with a configurable set of regexes and a small fuzzy matcher for API-like sequences; redaction will write a redaction-mask token and the masked content will be sent to an encrypted observability store accessible only via KMS-authorized workflows; (4) Add a compatibility shim in the HTTP/GRPC layer that, when SDK flag present, augments responses with X-Redwood-Chunk-Meta headers for older clients; (5) Wire metrics to Prometheus/grafana and export traces to OTLP collector.

Telemetry schema (draft): span.kind=server.request, chunk.span_id, chunk.parent_span_id, chunk_index, chunk_size_bytes, tokens, emit_latency_ms, redaction_applied (boolean), redaction_pattern_id. Store only pattern_id in plaintext logs; full redacted substring stored encrypted.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Full plaintext persistence simplifies debugging but violates compliance; we choose masked+encrypted approach for most customers. 2) Per-chunk spans increase cardinality in tracing backends — mitigate via sampling and span aggregation (rollup spans per-request after k chunks). 3) Redaction heuristics may over-redact; provide customer opt-in allowlist and audit log for redactions.
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with Observability and Runtime teams. Agreed on minimal schema and need for sampling strategy. Owners: Miguel (runtime), Priya (observability).

2026-02-26: Prototype middleware implemented in the emitter: emits OTLP event for chunk start/emit. Microbench shows +1.7% p50 latency on bench harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1582

2026-03-02: Security review stub completed. Initial redaction regex set drafted by security: (?:Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-\._~\+\/]+=*), 16\d{12,}, 0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}. Decision: use layered redaction (regex -> heuristic token classifier).
2026-03-05: SDK shim RFC posted and discussed — Node and Python SDK changes scoped. Backwards compatibility ensured via header-based opt-in. RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-streaming-shim

2026-03-09: End-to-end test harness created that validates redaction masks and encrypted storage roundtrip. Found bug: parent_span_id not propagated on GRPC streaming re-connects. Hotfix branch created. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/37
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind `streaming_chunk_telemetry`. Canary to 1% traffic for 48h with health checks: error_rate, trace_export_errors, redaction_failures. If metrics cross thresholds, auto-disable and alert on-call. Gradual ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with manual signoffs.
risks: High cardinality in tracing backend leading to increased costs
SDK compatibility edge-cases for older GRPC clients that don't preserve headers
mitigations: Implement adaptive sampling and span rollups for long streams
Add allowlist and a dry-run mode that logs redaction candidates without masking for customer validation
Provide server-side fallback to legacy telemetry if client shim not present and customer opts in
next_steps: Finish span propagation fix and merge hotfix branch (target 2026-03-11)
Complete Node/Python SDK shims and publish minor releases (target 2026-03-15)
Create Grafana dashboards and Grafana alert rules (target 2026-03-12)
Start canary rollout once observability pipelines are validated end-to-end
